findings.title: Options-object calls enable rejectOnClear by default despite documented default false
findings.cause: When pLimit receives an options object, the destructuring default is `rejectOnClear = true` even though the README and type declarations document `rejectOnClear` as optional with default `false`.
findings.impact: Any caller that switches from `pLimit(1)` to `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` without opting into rejection gets different clearQueue behavior: pending promises are rejected with AbortError instead of being discarded/unresolved. This can break Promise.all flows or surface unexpected unhandled rejections.
findings.evidence: Current source line 7 sets `rejectOnClear = true`; readme.md lines 46-52 and 149-155 plus index.d.ts lines 99-106 state the default is false. Focused runtime probe returned `defaultRejectOnClearStatus: rejected:AbortError` for `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` followed by `clearQueue()`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e 'import {setTimeout as delay} from "node:timers/promises"; import pLimit from "./index.js"; const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); limit(() => new Promise(() => {})); const pending = limit(() => "should not run"); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); console.log(await Promise.race([pending.then(v => `resolved:${v}`, e => `rejected:${e.name}`), delay(25, "pending")]));' prints `rejected:AbortError`; the documented/default behavior should leave it pending unless `rejectOnClear: true` is supplied.

findings.title: Falsey non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass runtime validation
findings.cause: The runtime check only throws when `rejectOnClear` is truthy and not a boolean: `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`.
findings.impact: Invalid configurations such as `rejectOnClear: 0`, `rejectOnClear: ''`, or `rejectOnClear: null` are silently accepted even though the public API says the option is boolean. That creates inconsistent validation where truthy invalid values throw but falsey invalid values alter behavior without warning.
findings.evidence: index.js line 12 gates validation on truthiness; readme.md lines 46-49 and index.d.ts lines 99-106 require a boolean. The focused probe recorded `invalidRejectOnClearAccepted: [0, empty-string, null]`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e 'import pLimit from "./index.js"; for (const value of [0, "", null]) { try { pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: value}); console.log("accepted", value); } catch (error) { console.log("threw", value, error.name); } }' shows all three invalid values are accepted.

findings.title: limit.map drops the mapper index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The mapper wrapper passes `index` only when `Array.isArray(iterable)` is true, and passes `undefined` for Set, generator, and iterator inputs.
findings.impact: The documented `limit.map(iterable, mapperFunction)` contract says the mapper receives the item value and its index for an iterable. Callers using Sets or iterators get `undefined` for the second argument, breaking index-dependent mapping while the current tests still pass because iterable tests ignore the index.
findings.evidence: index.js lines 107-112 conditionally pass `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`; readme.md lines 78-85 and index.d.ts lines 30-43 state the mapper receives an index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`. Runtime probe returned `mapArrayIndexes: [0, 1]` but `mapSetIndexes: [null, null]` because undefined array entries serialize as null.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e 'import pLimit from "./index.js"; const limit = pLimit(2); console.log(await limit.map(new Set(["a", "b"]), (_value, index) => index));' prints `[ undefined, undefined ]`; expected `[0, 1]`.

findings.title: limitFunction wrapper ignores all call arguments
findings.cause: The wrapper returned by `limitFunction` is now `() => limit(() => function_())`, so it neither accepts nor forwards `...arguments_` to the wrapped function.
findings.impact: Any limited function that depends on parameters is called with no arguments at runtime. This contradicts the type declaration and makes common wrappers such as `limitFunction(async id => fetch(id), options)` return wrong results.
findings.evidence: index.js line 124 drops arguments; index.d.ts lines 133-136 declare the returned function as `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`, and index.test-d.ts lines 24-26 exercise an argument-taking wrapper at the type level only. Focused runtime probe reported `resultType: undefined`, `isUndefined: true` for `limitFunction(async value => value)("argument-forwarded")`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e 'import {limitFunction} from "./index.js"; const limited = limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1}); console.log(await limited("argument-forwarded"));' prints `undefined`; expected `argument-forwarded`.

findings.title: Positive Infinity is no longer accepted as an unlimited concurrency value
findings.cause: The validator now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency) && concurrency > 0`, removing the explicit `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` branch that exists in HEAD.
findings.impact: Users can no longer pass `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` to effectively disable limiting while keeping the same API surface, and the concurrency setter rejects the same value. This is an edge-case regression from the repository baseline and conflicts with the error text/API idea of accepting numbers from 1 and up.
findings.evidence: git diff shows the validator changed from `((Number.isInteger(concurrency) || concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) && concurrency > 0)` to integer-only; current index.js line 128 throws. Focused probe returned `infinityConstructor: {created: false, error: "Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up"}`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e 'import pLimit from "./index.js"; try { console.log(pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY).concurrency); } catch (error) { console.log(error.message); }' prints `Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up`; the baseline accepts Infinity.
